title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - Stellar Convergence
next_steps: Share Redwood security one-pager and SOC2 report (Jordan)
Set up pilot technical kickoff for week of 2026-08-17 (Priya/Samir)
action_items: Jordan Lee: Update pipeline with expected close dates and ARR estimates (due_date: 2026-08-03)
Priya Nair: Run preliminary performance benchmark against Stellar's LLM workload and share results (due_date: 2026-08-12)
Marcus Hale: Provide customer list and contact for co-sell outreach (due_date: 2026-08-05)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-27
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (Stellar), Aisha Rahman (Stellar), Samir Patel (Stellar)
Shared: Co-sell pipeline spreadsheet (link), Redwood security one-pager (link), preliminary deck (link)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for making time, appreciate it. Quick audio check?
[00:10] Marcus Hale: Sounds good on my end, yep.
[00:15] Aisha Rahman: Good here.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Great. We're here to go through the joint pipeline and make sure we're aligned on priorities for co-selling, potential pilots, and any blockers — also to surface where Redwood Dedicated or Private might be the right fit.

[00:40] Priya Nair: I'll jump in on technical questions as they come. From a high level, we want to understand which deals are most likely to close in the next 60 days and what the technical gating items are.

[01:05] Marcus Hale: We have three prioritized accounts in the pipeline: Helios Health, Meridian Finance, and Orion Logistics. Helios is top — they care about data residency and SOC2. Meridian is more latency-sensitive, Orion has a heavy throughput embedding workload.

[02:10] Jordan Lee: Awesome. For Helios, sounds like Private or Dedicated with VPC will be needed; we should confirm whether their legal team will accept Redwood Private or they want on-prem. Do you know their compliance ask?

[02:35] Marcus Hale: They asked for ISO, SOC2 and audit logs. They also asked about KMS integration.

[02:50] Priya Nair: On KMS, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) — we can provide integration details. For SOC2 and audit logs we have the one-pager, I'll follow up with the artifacts.

[03:20] Aisha Rahman: For Meridian, latency is the top objection — they benchmarked against GalacticaCloud last quarter and liked the warm cache capabilities.

[03:40] Jordan Lee: Right, we should highlight our caching + batching controls and Redwood Dedicated's predictable latency SLOs. Priya can run a short perf sim with a similar seq len distribution to show tail-latency numbers.

[04:05] Priya Nair: I can do that — ideally I need a sample workload or at least token distribution, peak RPS numbers. Samir, can you help with that?

[04:20] Samir Patel: Yes, I can export an anonymized sample and send it. Expect that by EOD tomorrow.

[04:35] Jordan Lee: Perfect. On Orion Logistics, they asked about embedding scale and cost. We should propose Redwood Optimize suggestions — quantization profiles and batching — to reduce token costs. Also discuss multi-model routing if they have fallbacks.

[05:00] Marcus Hale: One thing to watch is procurement timelines — Helios indicated a procurement cycle that could take 8-10 weeks with legal.

[05:20] Jordan Lee: Ok that suggests we prioritize Meridian for a faster pilot if they can commit to a two-week POC. What would success criteria look like for them?

[05:35] Marcus Hale: For Meridian, success is 99th percentile latency under 120ms and cost per 1M tokens under $X (they gave a target). Also an integration with their SSO (SAML).

[06:00] Priya Nair: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC — will share the SSO integration guide. For the latency target, we'll run an internal sim and propose Dedicated slot sizing.

[06:25] Aisha Rahman: On co-sell motions, Stellar wants a joint case study and an intro to our sales reps for Helios. We'll need someone at Redwood to lead the exec brief.

[06:45] Jordan Lee: I'll own the exec brief and coordinate with growth. We'll put together a one-page co-sell plan for each prioritized account.

[07:05] Marcus Hale: Sounds good. A couple of questions from my side: what are Redwood's standard pricing tiers for Dedicated and what's the min commitment?

[07:20] Jordan Lee: For Dedicated we do reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. I'll send the pricing sheet but typical pilots can run on a short-term reserved burstable plan or trial credits to prove value before committing.

[07:40] Samir Patel: Tech deep dive — is there an option to run on premise? For Helios they might prefer on-prem due to data controls.

[07:50] Priya Nair: We offer Redwood Private with on-prem package as an option; that is more of an enterprise license + deployment project. It includes our control plane optionally in-customer VPC and KMS integrations. There is an implementation timeline to consider.

[08:15] Marcus Hale: Any known limitations for the on-prem package — like feature parity vs hosted?

[08:30] Priya Nair: Mostly parity for the inference runtime; the console/observability features can be configured to ship logs to customer endpoints. Certain managed observability features default to hosted telemetry but you can opt for self-hosted collectors. We'll share a short doc.

[09:00] Jordan Lee: Let's walk the pipeline spreadsheet now — I'll call out deal stages. (Jordan shares screen)

[09:20] Jordan Lee: Helios Health — stage: Contract Review, ARR estimate: $420k, next milestone is legal review. Owner: Marcus.

[09:45] Marcus Hale: Correct, legal review kickoff on 8/2 internally.

[10:00] Jordan Lee: Meridian Finance — stage: Pilot commit, ARR estimate: $150k, technical POC first. Owner: Stellar sales lead.

[10:20] Aisha Rahman: We're targeting a 2-week POC window starting 8/17 if Redwood can provide a test endpoint.

[10:40] Priya Nair: We can stand up a dedicated trial environment for the POC. Need to agree on test data, SSO, and expected throughput.

[11:00] Jordan Lee: Orion Logistics — stage: Qualification, ARR estimate: $90k, they want cost modeling on embeddings.

[11:15] Samir Patel: For embeddings cost modeling, we want recommendations on quantization and model variants.

[11:30] Priya Nair: We'll run cost sims and include Optimize recommendations — batch size, kv cache, quantization. Also note there are tradeoffs on quality vs 4-bit quantization, we'll provide evals.

[12:00] Marcus Hale: Procurement ask: can Redwood provide a draft MSA? Helios legal wants to see contract language.

[12:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, legal can share a redline-friendly MSA. I'll include that in the follow-up package.

[12:30] Aisha Rahman: On co-sell materials, Stellar wants a joint deck and an intro email template for outreach.

[12:45] Jordan Lee: We'll produce a template and a short joint deck tailored per account.

[13:05] Priya Nair: Quick note on performance: we can often keep 95th/99th tail latency down with persistent KV cache and continuous batching, but real numbers depend on seq length and concurrency.

[13:30] Jordan Lee: Any further technical risks to call out?

[13:40] Samir Patel: For Helios, data residency + audit logs are main risk. For Meridian, integration with their SSO and meeting the latency SLO are risks. For Orion, cost at scale for embeddings.

[14:05] Jordan Lee: Agreed. Priya, can you produce a short risk mitigation doc per account?

[14:15] Priya Nair: Yes, will do — risk mitigation + recommended config (Dedicated size, quantization, caching) per account.

[14:30] Marcus Hale: On the sales side, Stellar asks whether Redwood has a partner discount or co-sell incentive.

[14:40] Jordan Lee: We have standard partner programs and co-sell credits for qualified deals — I'll loop in partnerships to confirm exact incentives.

[15:00] Aisha Rahman: Are there references from similar healthcare deployments?

[15:10] Jordan Lee: We have a healthcare case study (anonymized) focusing on compliance and on-prem work — I'll share that link.

[15:25] Marcus Hale: Good. Timeline recap: Helios legal review starts 8/2, Meridian POC week of 8/17, exec briefing 8/10.

[15:40] Jordan Lee: I'll send calendar invites for the exec brief and Meridian kickoff. Marcus, you'll share the anonymized sample and Stellar will prepare the outreach list.

[16:00] Samir Patel: I'll get the sample and baseline metrics by tomorrow EOD.

[16:15] Priya Nair: Follow-ups I will do: perf sim for Meridian and risk mitigation doc for three accounts.

[16:30] Jordan Lee: Great. Any final questions?

[16:40] Aisha Rahman: One ask — can Redwood provide a short checklist for procurement (required security artifacts)? That helps speed legal review.

[16:55] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have a procurement checklist — I'll attach it to the follow-up along with SOC2 and MSA.

[17:10] Marcus Hale: Thanks everyone.

[17:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks team. Quick recap of next steps and action items. Marcus to share sample and contact list, Priya to run perf tests, Jordan to send pricing, security docs, and schedule exec brief.

[17:40] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-attributions and small ASR errors; some technical terms spelled phonetically (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of KV cache).
